items.title: What to know about the US trial over Mamta Kafle’s disappearance

items.desc: With their homes and belongings reduced to ashes, families in Badgama and Mainakaderi are relying on emergency aid while facing the daunting cost of rebuilding.

items.desc: She is the first Nepali woman scientist and only the second Nepali citizen to receive the distinction.

items.title: Can Nepal’s hydropower boom withstand a changing Himalaya?

items.title: Mass protests in France spiral into worst riots in years
items.desc: More than half a million people took to the streets over rising living costs and deteriorating public services, as looting, arson and clashes with police left hundreds injured and led to 1,200 arrests.

items.title: Three women killed, three missing as jeep plunges into Sunkoshi
items.desc: The Tata Sumo jeep fell about 200 metres from the Mid-Hill Highway into the river in Sindhuli at 2:30am on Sunday. Four passengers, including the driver, were rescued.

items.title: Fiction: He was the best in class. He still wasn’t good enough
items.desc: When Eklavya is denied an award he has earned, he discovers that talent alone cannot overcome the prejudices of those in power.

items.desc: Says his main challenge was to preserve Congress’s legacy while making it relevant to a changing Nepali society.

items.title: Journalist Shrestha released after artist Panta agrees to approach Press Council
items.desc: Police had taken Shrestha from his residence to Cyber Bureau following a complaint over a report concerning the alleged takeover of 10-ropani land in Dhading.

items.title: Audio attributed to fugitive GB Rai says he is ready to face authorities
items.desc: In an audio recording and statement published by Setopati, Rai says he is ready to cooperate with authorities and repay depositors, but police have yet to authenticate the material.

items.title: Ani Choying Drolma appointed vice-chair of Lumbini Development Trust
items.desc: The Buddhist nun and singer was appointed by the Cabinet on October 16, following a proposal from the Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation. The post had been vacant for an extended period.

items.title: Nepal suffer shock defeat to Canada ahead of crucial Oman clash
items.desc: Yuvraj Samra’s maiden ODI century helped Canada secure a 24-run victory, leaving Nepal with one match remaining in the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup League 2.

items.title: Gagan Thapa tops vote count in Nepali Congress convention
items.desc: Lalitpur Mayor Chiribabu Maharjan ranks second among the top 10 vote-getters, followed by Basana Thapa, according to the results.

items.title: Banks to keep select branches open during Dashain holiday
items.desc: Customers will be able to make basic transactions at designated branches, with most banks planning to operate for two to three hours a day except on the day of Tika.

items.title: Bank stocks lead market rally, but can the gains last?

items.title: Police take journalist Kishor Shrestha to Cyber Bureau for talks over complaints
items.desc: Ruling RSP leader Himesh Panta filed a complaint over a report alleging his family had grabbed land, while Shrestha lodged a counter-complaint over Panta’s social media remarks.

items.title: How electric cooking can drive equity
items.desc: The failure to expand electric cooking in Nepali kitchens shows how Nepal’s energy policies are failing its people.

items.title: Nepal’s maternal healthcare system has a blind spot
items.desc: Nepal’s shift to fewer, stronger maternal facilities is sound. The floods show those facilities also have to hold up in a disaster.

items.title: Media outlets dress up for Dashain. What about other festivals?
items.desc: Dashain’s prominence in Nepali media is understandable, but how consistently do news outlets recognise the festivals of other religious and cultural communities?

items.title: Nepal’s leaders call for unity as Shah highlights Dashain’s financial strain
items.desc: Prime Minister Balendra Shah said financial hardship should not make the festival a burden, while the president and vice-president stressed social harmony and support for families affected by disasters.

items.title: Dashain paints the country in festive colours
items.desc: Crowded markets, kite-filled skies and packed roads capture the excitement as families head home and communities prepare to celebrate.

items.title: Shoppers crowd Kathmandu markets for Phulpati
items.desc: Families flock to traditional bazaars for flowers, sugarcane, ginger plants and other offerings used in the Dashain ritual.

items.title: Nepal’s cultural heritage finds new expression on the runway
items.desc: At NCFT’s graduating show, 54 designers focused on Nepal’s architecture, agricultural traditions, and traditional jewellery.
